correctness.rationale: The centered process is a linear filter of telegraph noise plus independent Gaussian thermal noise. Work random part equals −ω∫gσ−√(2D)∫g dB; Gaussian term has vanishing fourth cumulant. For s1<s2<s3<s4 the stationary telegraph fourth joint cumulant is exactly −2 exp{−γ[(s3−s1)+(s4−s2)]}, verified independently from all three pairings. Integrating it gives −48ω⁴ times an ordered positive-kernel integral. Nontrivial monotone finite-variation λ makes g nonzero and one-signed, proving strict negativity. For optimal initial/final jumps and linear interior, g=c(2e^(ks) for s<0,1 for 0≤s≤T); the A,B,C,J cascade has C→1/(2γ³), J=T/(2γ³)+O(1). Combined with Q=2T/γ+O(1), this yields the stated kurtosis coefficient after c cancels. For cyclic ±a jumps at separation δ, k→∞ gives 4(1−e^(−γδ))(3e^(−γδ)−1) by exact two-state parity, so short δ yields positive sign for sufficiently large finite k. Independently checked four-time cumulants, pulse-sign formula and Gaussian cancellation; inspected original standalone checker’s independent Markov moment recursion.
residual_risks: The strict sign only covers deterministic nonconstant monotone protocols, finite variation and stationary symmetric telegraph propulsion.
The cyclic result is an existence statement for sufficiently large stiffness at fixed short δ, not a complete finite-k sign classification.

value.rationale: A strict fourth-cumulant sign law for all monotone drive protocols, sharp contrast with cyclic reversal and Gaussian propulsion, and a concrete long-time coefficient resolve a motivated non-Gaussian work-fluctuation question beyond the known optimum/variance.
residual_risks: Physically model-specific, but the sign boundary covers an infinite-dimensional class of admissible protocols.

final_claim: For stationary telegraph propulsion in a translated harmonic trap, every nonconstant monotone finite-variation protocol has strictly negative fourth work cumulant; a two-jump reversal can have positive cumulant. The mean-work-optimal protocol has exact ordered-integral cumulant and standardized excess kurtosis −6ω⁴/[γ³(D+ω²/γ)²] T⁻¹+O(T⁻²).
limitations: The strict sign only covers deterministic nonconstant monotone protocols, finite variation and stationary symmetric telegraph propulsion.
The cyclic result is an existence statement for sufficiently large stiffness at fixed short δ, not a complete finite-k sign classification.
